Q: Return 444 if https port(443) accesed via http A:

If you want Nginx to close the connection with 444 instead of returning "The plain HTTP request was sent to HTTPS port", you can handle the internal 497 error with error_page:

# 497 = HTTP request sent to HTTPS port
# Reference: https://serverfault.com/questions/1067010/return-444-instead-of-400
error_page 497 =444 @close;

location @close {
    return 444;
}

However, this only affects requests that are recognized as plain HTTP on an HTTPS port. Random or malformed bytes can still result in 400 Bad Request.

To close the connection for both cases, include 400 in the error_page directive as well:

# 497 = HTTP request sent to HTTPS port
# 400 = Bad Request (malformed data)
error_page 497 400 =444 @close;

location @close {
    return 444;
}

And... Another case to be aware of is a plain-text CONNECT request sent directly to the HTTPS port, for example:

$ nc -v 127.0.0.1 443
Connection to 127.0.0.1 443 port [tcp/https] succeeded!
CONNECT 127.0.0.1:80 HTTP/1.0

HTTP/1.1 405 Not Allowed
Server: nginx
...

By default, Nginx short-circuits the request and responds with 405 Not Allowed.

If you also want these requests to be closed with 444, include 405 in the error_page directive:

⚠️ Don't copy this blindly. Only include the status codes that match your use case.

# 497 = HTTP request sent to HTTPS port
# 400 = Bad Request (malformed data)
# 405 = Not Allowed method (e.g. CONNECT) -- also affects valid HTTPS request
error_page 400 405 497 =444 @close;

location @close {
    return 444;
}

BUT it will also affect valid HTTPS requests that successfully complete the TLS handshake but use an unsupported HTTP method. So including 405 will have side effects.

For that reason, this config may only be suitable for a default server that is intended to silently drop unexpected or unknown traffic.

This covers the most common unwanted requests:

  • 497 — plain HTTP sent to an HTTPS port.
  • 400 — malformed or non-HTTP data.
  • 405 — unsupported methods such as CONNECT.

Q: Checking if key is being held down A:

You are going to get a call to _input per input event. And the event object you get as parameter in _input represents that single input.

If want to to this with the event object, it would be something like this:

func _input(event):
    if event.is_action_pressed("multi_build"):
        build_mode = true
    if event.is_action_released("multi_build"):
        build_mode = false

Alternatively, you can use Input to check if the action is currently pressed: Input.is_action_pressed("multi_build").

Q: Tosca XML Ressource - more than one control found for action "XML node" A:

You need to constrain, meaning you need to tell it which item you want to compare. In your case that would be the index. Find more about it here: https://documentation.tricentis.com/en/1200/index.htm#engines_3.0/api/api_tc_lists.htm?Highlight=constrain

Q: MaybeEncodingError: Error sending result: '<multiprocessing.pool.ExceptionWithTraceback object at 0x0000018F09F334A8>' A:

From the accepted answer, I understood that it is simply replacing from multiprocessing import Pool by from multiprocessing.dummy import Pool.

This worked for me.

Q: How to convert an XML schema (XSD) to Relax NG? A:

The old Sun RELAX NG Converter is nowadays bundled with the (Sun) 'Multi-Schema Validator' - msv. With that term you can search in your distributions package repository.

For example Fedora (e.g. 17) includes it.

Install on Fedora

# yum install msv-rngconv msv-manual

Usage on Fedora

$ rngconv my.xsd > my.rng

Test the result:

$ xmllint --relaxng my.rng --noout some.xml

Conversion to compact syntax:

$ trang -I rng -O rnc my.rng my.rnc

(trang is also available via the main Fedora package repository)

The other way (perhaps after adding stuff to the compact syntax file):

$ trang -I rnc -O rng my.rnc my.rng

Msv seems to be quite powerful - I tested it with a fairly sized xsd file that uses inheritance, extensive patterns and includes another xsd file.

Q: Does Firebird have an addition assignment operator? A:

No, Firebird doesn't have compound assignment operators.

However, specifically for blobs, Firebird 4.0.2 and higher have BLOB_APPEND which can be used for a form of compound assignment.
